headline: Cabinet approves draft law to curb online gambling, betting and match-fixing
summary: The Bangladeshi government is moving to crack down on illegal betting platforms and sports manipulation to protect citizens from financial loss.
details: The Cabinet has officially approved a draft law aimed at curbing online gambling, betting, and match-fixing across the country.
This new legislative move is designed to target illegal gambling operations that have proliferated through digital platforms.
The draft law specifically addresses the risks associated with online betting, which often leads to significant financial losses for users.
Additionally, the law focuses on match-fixing, aiming to protect the integrity of sports and prevent corruption in athletic competitions.
Once the law is passed by Parliament, it will provide legal frameworks for authorities to monitor and block illegal betting sites.
The government's action comes amid growing concerns over the rise of unregulated gambling apps and websites targeting young people.

Once the law is passed by Parliament, it will provide legal frameworks for authorities to monitor and block illegal betting sites.

The government's action comes amid growing concerns over the rise of unregulated gambling apps and websites targeting young people.

headline: Over 60,000 Bangladeshi Hajj pilgrims return home, 54 die during pilgrimage
summary: Over 60,000 nationals have returned from Saudi Arabia, while 54 pilgrims died during the journey, according to the Ministry of Religious Affairs.
details: Over 60,588 Bangladeshi nationals have returned home after performing Hajj, according to the latest bulletin from the Ministry of Religious Affairs.
Among the returnees, 4,319 pilgrims traveled on government packages, while 56,269 used private arrangements.
A total of 152 return flights operated, with Biman Bangladesh Airlines carrying 26,868 pilgrims, Saudia Airlines carrying 21,045, and Flynas carrying 8,672.
Tragically, 54 Bangladeshis died during the pilgrimage in Saudi Arabia, including 36 men and 18 women.
Of the deceased, 37 died in Makkah, 16 in Madinah, and one in Jeddah. No deaths were recorded in Mina, Arafa, or Muzdalifah.
The Ministry of Religion reports that 66,249 automatic medical prescriptions were issued and 415 pilgrims received treatment at local hospitals.
Currently, 15 pilgrims are still undergoing treatment in various hospitals in Saudi Arabia.
For comparison, 48 people died during the Hajj last year, and the highest death count in recent years was 121 in 2023.
caption:
Over 60,000 Bangladeshi Hajj pilgrims have returned home, but 54 lives were lost during the pilgrimage.

Over 60,588 Bangladeshi nationals have returned home after performing Hajj, according to the latest bulletin from the Ministry of Religious Affairs.

Among the returnees, 4,319 pilgrims traveled on government packages, while 56,269 used private arrangements.

A total of 152 return flights operated, with Biman Bangladesh Airlines carrying 26,868 pilgrims, Saudia Airlines carrying 21,045, and Flynas carrying 8,672.

Tragically, 54 Bangladeshis died during the pilgrimage in Saudi Arabia, including 36 men and 18 women.

Of the deceased, 37 died in Makkah, 16 in Madinah, and one in Jeddah. No deaths were recorded in Mina, Arafa, or Muzdalifah.

The Ministry of Religion reports that 66,249 automatic medical prescriptions were issued and 415 pilgrims received treatment at local hospitals.

Currently, 15 pilgrims are still undergoing treatment in various hospitals in Saudi Arabia.

For comparison, 48 people died during the Hajj last year, and the highest death count in recent years was 121 in 2023.
